name: Seoul Walkability: Four Pairwise Dimensions
description:
Method replication: participants compare two Seoul street views and pick the better one, or Tie, for safety, comfort, pleasurability and overall walkability (4 parts, 10 pairs each), without being given definitions, then may describe the criteria they used; the images are not the paper's stimuli (57 Google Street View images of Seoul streets, 2017–2019, fetched for this template).
Original study: Yoo, Cho & Kim (2026), "Explaining walkability with a zero-shot multimodal LLM: Validation and empirical application", Sustainable Cities and Society 144, 107431. 200 Naver Street View images from five land-use types in Seoul (2022 and 2024) formed five pair sets; fifteen experts with doctorates in urban planning fields, three per set, chose the better image or a tie on each dimension with no definitions or rubrics, then described their criteria. Their judgements served as the benchmark for a zero-shot GPT-4o assessment.
Differences from the original study: (1) Google Street View images instead of Naver, from random Seoul street points rather than balanced land-use samples, and including some larger roads; (2) each of the four dimensions uses its own random pairs, instead of judging all four dimensions on the same pair; (3) 10 pairs per dimension instead of a fixed set of pairs per expert; (4) open to anyone, with a question about planning background instead of an expert-only panel.
author: Yoo, Cho & Kim
